newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel asks EU not to infringe Palestinian deal.
newsitem.headline: Israel asks EU not to infringe Palestinian deal.

text.p: Israel has asked the European Union not to infringe on the economic agreement between Israel and the Palestinian Authority while negotiating an economic agreement with the Palestinians.

Oded Eran, Foreign Ministry deputy director general for economic affairs, said on Sunday the agreements signed between Israel and the Palestinians in 1994 do not allow the Authority to sign separate economic agreements with foreign governments, such as trade deals.

Recently EU foreign ministers gave the European Commission a mandate to negotiate the Palestinian Authority's entry to the Euromed accord, which governs the 15-nation block's relations with its Mediterranean partners.
"Canada and the United States for example have decided to extend to the Palestinian Authority the same free trade agreements they have with us," he told Reuters.
"The Europeans can do the same," he said.
But he added: "I don't know the details of the mandate (that the EU foreign ministers gave to the European Commission), but it must not conflict with the agreements we have with the Palestinians."
Eran said Foreign Minister David Levy had recently raised the issue in talks with Europe's foreign ministers and said Israel will continue to raise the issue in future talks as well.
The economic agreement signed by Israel and the Palestinians in 1994 saw the establishement of a customs union between the two sides.
